pointers.sentence: Since 6.0 it is to be a tuple, for "the interoperability problems that resulted", the notes say (`docs/releases/6.0.txt`).

At this commit `Func.as_sql` and `Col.as_sql` return tuples, and `BuiltinLookup.as_sql` unpacks both halves into one, so a half of either kind still joins (`django/db/models/expressions.py:Func.as_sql`, `django/db/models/lookups.py:BuiltinLookup.as_sql`).

Until 6.1 `SQLCompiler.quote_name_unless_alias` left such an alias bare; since then `Col.as_sql`, `BaseTable.as_sql` and `Join.as_sql` write every name through `SQLCompiler.quote_name` (`django/db/models/sql/datastructures.py:Join.as_sql`, `django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:SQLCompiler.quote_name`).

Until 6.1 `SQLCompiler.quote_name_unless_alias` left such an alias bare; since then `Col.as_sql`, `BaseTable.as_sql` and `Join.as_sql` write every name through `SQLCompiler.quote_name` (`django/db/models/sql/datastructures.py:Join.as_sql`, `django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:SQLCompiler.quote_name`).
The notes give the reason, collisions with special characters, and warn that a quoted alias is case-sensitive, so raw SQL naming one of mixed case may need quoting (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).
The select list's alias, `"Calm__title"`, is quoted under every release: what 6.1 quoted are the aliases of tables and joins (`django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:SQLCompiler.as_sql`).

`SQLCompiler.quote_name_unless_alias` is deprecated since 6.1; it warns with `RemovedInDjango2028Warning` and quotes whatever it is given: a join's alias, `'T3'` until 6.0.8, comes back `'"T3"'` on SQLite (`django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:SQLCompiler.quote_name_unless_alias`; [The compiler: `as_sql`, `execute_sql` and `results_iter`](../sql/compiler.md)).

A percent sign in an alias is deprecated since 6.0: `Query.check_alias` warns with `RemovedInDjango2028Warning` and accepts it, as 5.2.17 did without a word (`django/db/models/sql/query.py:Query.check_alias`; [The SELECT clause: `get_select`, the select mask and `klass_info`](../sql/select.md)).

Aggregates came into `django.db.models` in two releases: `StringAgg` and the bit aggregates, `BitAnd`, `BitOr` and `BitXor`, from the PostgreSQL application, and `AnyValue`, which no earlier release had (`django/db/models/aggregates.py:StringAgg`, `django/db/models/aggregates.py:BitAggregate`).

Aggregates came into `django.db.models` in two releases: `StringAgg` and the bit aggregates, `BitAnd`, `BitOr` and `BitXor`, from the PostgreSQL application, and `AnyValue`, which no earlier release had (`django/db/models/aggregates.py:StringAgg`, `django/db/models/aggregates.py:BitAggregate`).

`AnyValue` is refused with `NotSupportedError` where `BaseDatabaseFeatures.supports_any_value` is off, as on MariaDB, and the bit aggregates where `BaseDatabaseFeatures.supports_bit_aggregations` is off, as on Oracle before 21 (`django/db/models/aggregates.py:AnyValue.as_sql`).
On SQLite 6.1 lets `StringAgg` take `distinct=True` with the delimiter `Value(",")` only (`django/db/models/aggregates.py:StringAgg.as_sqlite`).
Since 6.0 `Aggregate.__init__` takes an order_by argument, refused with `TypeError` unless the class sets `Aggregate.allow_order_by` (`django/db/models/aggregates.py:Aggregate.__init__`).
5.2's filter_template, which wrapped any template in `" FILTER (WHERE ...)"`, is gone, which the 6.0 notes do not say (`django/db/models/aggregates.py:Aggregate.as_sql`).

The reference documentation at this commit still gives `Aggregate.template` as `"%(function)s(%(distinct)s%(expressions)s)"`, and its example aggregate has no slot for the filter (`docs/ref/models/expressions.txt`).
Since 5.2 `Func.__init__` refuses `Avg`, `Max`, `Min` and `Sum` any number of arguments but one with `TypeError`, through `Func.arity` (`django/db/models/expressions.py:Func.__init__`).

`Count`, `StdDev` and `Variance`, which the 5.2 notes name too, take a second as the filter or as sample; `Count("title", "published")` fails under 5.2.17 with `AttributeError`, and from 6.0 takes the field published as its filter (`django/db/models/aggregates.py:Count.__init__`).
To a `JSONField` a `None` saved is SQL's `"NULL"`, and a `None` compared with the whole value is JSON's null (`django/db/models/fields/json.py:JSONField.get_db_prep_save`).

6.1 added `JSONNull`, which is JSON's null in both places, and deprecated the `None` compared with the whole value, the top-level `None`: `JSONExact.process_rhs` warns with `RemovedInDjango2028Warning` and compiles it as before (`django/db/models/expressions.py:JSONNull`, `django/db/models/fields/json.py:JSONExact.process_rhs`).

When it ends, the 6.1 notes say (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`), a top-level `None` compiles to `"IS NULL"` and a key's is unaffected ([From a name to a column: `names_to_path`, `setup_joins` and `build_lookup`](../sql/names.md)).
Until 6.1 `iexact=None` on a key was `isnull=True` on it; since 6.1 `KeyTransformIExact.as_sql` compiles it as `exact=None` (`django/db/models/fields/json.py:KeyTransformIExact.as_sql`).

`BaseDatabaseOperations.compile_json_path` refuses one where `BaseDatabaseFeatures.supports_json_negative_indexing` is off, as on MySQL (`django/db/backends/base/operations.py:BaseDatabaseOperations.compile_json_path`; [The SQL a backend writes: `BaseDatabaseOperations`](../backends/operations.md)).
